Approximately 13% of the US adults have type two diabetes, representing a significant burden on public health in the United States. Type two diabetes is approximately twice as prevalent in African-Americans as in European-Americans. in the multithnic cohort. This racial and ethnic difference persisted after
[00:34:06] stratification by body mass index. Data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey confirmed the substantial racial disparity in diabetes across the United States. In the atherosclerosis risk in communities study, African-Americans are twice as likely as whites to develop incident type 2 diabetes, a disparity which persists even after extensive adjustments for socioeconomic status and behavioral risk factors. This persistent disparity suggests that genetic factors may contribute to ethnic differences in susceptibility to type two diabetes.
